scope: Independent metadata, theory and official-template audit; no report edits

references.title: Numerical Optimization
references.claims: The book provides the standard unconstrained optimization, line-search, CG and quasi-Newton background. Bibliographic data and chapter coverage verified on the publisher page; full copyrighted book text was not downloaded. The report GD bound and curvature inequality were independently checked algebraically.

references.title: Minimization of functions having Lipschitz continuous first partial derivatives
references.claims: The primary article supports the historical sufficient-decrease and variable-step gradient-method attribution. Its stronger convergence statements have explicit additional assumptions; the report does not incorrectly claim those original statements for arbitrary nonconvex functions. Sentence-case versus publisher all-caps title is not a metadata error.

references.title: Global Convergence Properties of Conjugate Gradient Methods for Optimization
references.claims: Publisher abstract concerns two safeguarded CG families, practical line searches and smooth nonconvex functions. It does not justify arbitrary PR+ unconditionally. SciPy source lines 1616–1650 independently confirm the PR+ truncation and extra sufficient-descent check, with sigma_3=0.01 and a gradient-tolerance exception. Current report wording is appropriately qualified.

references.title: A new approach to variable metric algorithms
references.claims: Author, title, year, volume, issue, pages and DOI match the publisher-indexed record. Direct page access intermittently fails, but the primary publisher search result provides the metadata and abstract. Describing it as part of the variable-metric/BFGS foundation is accurate.

references.title: Non-asymptotic Global Convergence Analysis of BFGS with the Armijo-Wolfe Line Search
references.booktitle: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
references.claims: Assumptions 2.1–2.2 require twice differentiability, global mu-strong convexity and L-Lipschitz gradient. Hessian Lipschitz continuity (Assumption 2.3) supports stronger rates. Initial Hessian approximation is positive definite; Armijo parameter is below 1/2. Weak Wolfe is analyzed and stronger Wolfe also qualifies. Rates cannot be applied globally to these nonconvex benchmarks. Current report states that limitation correctly.
references.optional_improvement: Add pages 16810–16851 and DOI 10.52202/079017-0536; preserve 2024 conference year separately from the January 2025 author-version revision.

references.title: A Globalization of L-BFGS and the Barzilai–Borwein Method for Nonconvex Unconstrained Optimization
references.journal: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
references.claims: Theorem 4.2 gives stationary cluster points for modified LBFGSM under Assumption 4.1. Gradient-norm convergence uses stronger uniform-continuity/boundedness conditions. Theorem 4.4 additionally needs local strong convexity, locally Lipschitz gradient and calibrated cautious-update parameters; it gives q-linear objective and eventual l-step q-linear iterate/gradient behavior. These are not guarantees for ordinary SciPy full-memory BFGS. Current report makes no invalid transfer.

references.author: SciPy developers
references.title: CG/BFGS documentation and scipy/optimize/_optimize.py
references.claims: Versioned docs support Euclidean norm selection, gtol, c1/c2, xrtol and the identity initial inverse Hessian. Source confirms CG safeguard and generic dense A1*H*A2 BFGS update. O(d^3) is a conventional dense-arithmetic inference, not an empirical scaling result; current report identifies it as such.
references.optional_improvement: Include the versioned optimize tutorial in this grouped reference to support the specific Rosenbrock model and known optimum.

references.title: Virtual Library of Simulation Experiments: Test Functions and Datasets — Rastrigin Function
references.claims: The cited page is specifically Rastrigin and supports the multimodal benchmark description. It is not a dedicated Rosenbrock reference. Website access-date citation without an invented publication year is acceptable. The stable sine-squared form and unique zero minimizer also follow directly from the displayed nonnegative sum.
references.citation_precision_improvement: For the introduction statement about both functions, cite [7,8] after adding the SciPy Rosenbrock tutorial to [7], or cite benchmark geometry separately. Do not rely on the SFU Rosenbrock page generic unimodality description for higher-dimensional claims.

overall: All eight references are real and their supplied author/year/title/venue metadata is accurate. No invalid transfer of recent convex or modified-LBFGS theorems was found. Citation targeting and optional complete conference metadata can be improved.

precise_fixes.location: Introduction citation [1,8] on both benchmark functions
precise_fixes.fix: Use dedicated SciPy Rosenbrock tutorial in [7] and cite [7,8], or split the references by function. This is a targeting improvement, not evidence that either benchmark claim is false.
Add conference pages 16810–16851 and DOI 10.52202/079017-0536 from official BibTeX.
Current ReportLab A4/507pt-width/10.3pt/13.1pt leading layout is custom, not the official NeurIPS 2025 template. Do not label it exact NeurIPS formatting.

official_neurips_2025_template.direct_sty_tex_urls: Four plausible standalone media URLs returned 404. The canonical official source is the zip linked from the CFP; do not invent a direct file URL.
official_neurips_2025_template.identity: Default review mode anonymizes. A named course submission requires an author-showing option such as preprint; do not imply conference acceptance with an inappropriate camera-ready label.
official_neurips_2025_template.course_precedence: Course PDF encourages NeurIPS 2025 but does not mandate it. Course maximum 10 pages, PDF under 20MB, name and student ID at beginning and Canvas submission take priority. Conference-only 9-content-page/reference exemptions, 50MB and checklist rules do not replace course rules.
